defect: The v1 plan pinned tokenizer.json (10,115,786 B), vocab.json (3,032,795 B) and merges.txt (1,567,883 B) with retain=false, so the captured bundle hashed and discarded them; offline reproduction could never supply the tokenizer payloads a later Spark adapter needs.
changes: configs/spark_source_preparation_v2.json: retain=true for those six pinned payloads (three per official source); all sha256/byte pins unchanged from v1.

HARD_MAX_PER_FILE_RETAIN_BYTES raised 8 MiB -> 16 MiB, aligned with the plan max_asset_bytes bound, so the pinned fast-tokenizer payload is retainable; every retained asset is still hash- and size-verified.

export_header_bundle(): authors header_bundle.json from a completed run's verified sidecars; scripts/prepare_spark_sources.py --export-header-bundle exposes it. Offline reruns are now provisionable from one completed run.

provisioning_run.network: 39 bounded requests, 29,708,060 bytes fetched, weights never downloaded, remote code never executed

offline_reproduction.verification: All six tokenizer/vocab/merges payloads byte-identical between run_02 and run_03 and sha256-matched to the plan pins.

fingerprint_difference_cause: manifest_fingerprint covers generated_at, fetch_policy and provenance records, which legitimately differ between the online provisioning run and the offline reproduction (network flags, etags, record provenance). Asset digests and inventories are identical.
limits: Preparation only. No Spark native execution, adapter qualification, weight download or FP8 training claim; large payloads stay in the gitignored data/cache external cache.
